title: Coordinate description of the maximal branch stratum
statement: Let $U$ be a regular locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $t_1,\ldots,t_s$ be regular functions on $U$, with $s\geq 1$. Suppose that for every point $u\in U$, the germs of exactly those $t_j$ vanishing at $u$ are distinct members of a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{U,u}$; a regular system of parameters of a regular local ring of dimension $d$ means $d$ generators of its maximal ideal. Put $D_U=V(\prod_{j=1}^s t_j)$ and $C=V(t_1,\ldots,t_s)$, as closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For a geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, put $b(\bar u)=\#\{j:t_j(u)=0\text{ in }\kappa(u)\}$. This is the number of geometric local branches of $D_U$, equivalently the number of minimal primes of the reduced strict henselian local ring of $D_U$ at $\bar u$, with branch number zero off $D_U$. It is unchanged on passing to an etale neighborhood [def-weil-etale-morphism] and is independent of a choice of such coordinate equations. For every integer $k$, the subset $\{b\geq k\}$ is the union of the coordinate intersections $V(t_j:j\in J)$ with $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$ and $|J|=k$ (all of $U$ for $k\leq0$, empty for $k>s$). In particular $b\leq s$, and $b=s$ exactly on $C$. The closed subscheme $C$ is regular and reduced, and is permitted to be empty; the value $s$ is attained if and only if $C$ is nonempty. The same assertions hold after every etale base change. Here the reduced strict henselian local ring at a geometric point is the reduction of the filtered colimit of local rings of its pointed etale neighborhoods, and a minimal prime is a prime ideal minimal under inclusion.

proof.text: Fix $u\in U$ and put $A=\mathcal O_{U,u}$ and $I_u=\{j:t_j\in\mathfrak m_A\}$. The other factors are units. By [def-weil-regular-scheme], $A$ is a regular Noetherian local ring. Extend the factors indexed by $I_u$ to a regular system of parameters. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], after any permutation every quotient by an initial subfamily is regular local, and the remaining parameters are successive nonzerodivisors. In particular $A/(t_j)$ is regular local for $j\in I_u$. Let $H=A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for the separable closure selected by $\bar u$. The geometric-to-algebraic presentation [lem-sbc-geometric-strict-henselization-local-presentation] identifies this with the strict local ring at $\bar u$: on an affine chart the prime is $u$, as seen by contracting the kernel of the residue map induced by $\bar u$. Apply [lem-sbc-strict-henselization-surjective-quotient] to $A\twoheadrightarrow A/(t_j)$: its kernel lies in $\mathfrak m_A$, so $H/t_jH$ is a strict henselization of $A/(t_j)$. It is regular local by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular], and a nonzero domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. Thus $P_j=t_jH$ is a proper prime ideal.

proof.text:
For distinct $i,j\in I_u$, reorder the parameter system with $t_j$ first and $t_i$ second. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $t_i$ is a nonzerodivisor in the nonzero ring $A/(t_j)$, hence $t_i
otin(t_j)$. The map $A	o H$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], $t_i
otin t_jH$. Thus the primes $P_j$ of Step 1 are pairwise incomparable. Put $F=\prod_{j\in I_u}t_j$. If $I_u$ is nonempty, the local ring of $D_U$ at $u$ is $A/(F)$, since discarded factors are units. By [lem-sbc-strict-henselization-surjective-quotient] its strict henselization is $H/(F)H$, identified with its geometric strict local ring by [lem-sbc-geometric-strict-henselization-local-presentation]. Every prime of $H$ containing $F$ contains some $t_j$, hence contains $P_j$. Conversely each $P_j$ contains $F$; incomparability shows that these, and only these, are the primes minimal over $(F)H$. Passing to the quotient and then killing nilpotents does not change this prime poset: every prime contains each nilpotent, and inverse image along the quotient is an inclusion-preserving bijection onto primes containing its kernel. Consequently the reduced strict local ring of $D_U$ has exactly $|I_u|$ minimal primes. When $I_u$ is empty, $F=1$ and $u
otin D_U$, giving branch number zero by convention. This proves the intrinsic description of $b$ and its independence of coordinate equations.

proof.text: For $u\in C$, all $s$ factors are in $\mathfrak m_A$ and form part of a regular system of parameters, so $s\le\dim A$. The closed-subscheme description [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies $\mathcal O_{C,u}$ with $A/(t_1,\ldots,t_s)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] this ring is regular local. The scheme $C$ is locally Noetherian: on an affine Noetherian chart of $U$ its ring is the quotient by the finitely generated ideal of the restricted functions, and ideals in a quotient correspond to ideals containing the kernel, so ascending chains stabilize. Hence [def-weil-regular-scheme] implies that $C$ is regular. Every displayed local ring is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]; a nilpotent in a domain is zero, so [def-pc-reduced-scheme] implies that $C$ is reduced. If $C$ is empty these local assertions hold vacuously.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.8, printed p.118: regularity of the deepest stratum; coordinate intersections as in 4.2.4, printed p.119. Stacks Tag 00NQ for the quotient rings.

proof.text: For $1\le k\le s$, the finite set $I_u$ has at least $k$ elements if and only if it contains a subset $J$ of cardinality $k$. For that $J$, every $t_j$, $j\in J$, has zero residue at $u$, which is exactly membership in $V(t_j:j\in J)$ by the closed-subscheme equations [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This proves the asserted union formula. For $k\le0$ the inequality holds at every point; for $k>s$ it holds nowhere. There are only finitely many subsets $J$, so each nontrivial union is closed. Taking $k=s$ gives $b=s$ exactly on the underlying set of $C$, and $0\le b\le s$ follows from $I_u\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$. Therefore $s$ occurs if and only if $C$ has a point; a geometric point above any such point is obtained by taking an algebraic closure of its residue field.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.6 and 4.1.8, printed p.118: finite coordinate description of multiplicity loci and deepest stratum.

proof.text: Let $v:W\to U$ be any etale morphism and let $w\mapsto u$. It is locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence locally of finite type (finite presentation supplies finitely many algebra generators). Thus $W$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. Work on affine etale charts and put $A=\mathcal O_{U,u}$, $B=\mathcal O_{W,w}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal], $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$, and by [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension], $\dim B=\dim A=d$. A $d$-element regular system of parameters of $A$ therefore maps to $d$ generators of $\mathfrak m_B$. By the definition [def-weil-regular-scheme], $B$ is regular local and those images form a regular system of parameters. The images of the factors vanishing at $u$ occupy distinct positions in this system. Precisely these factors vanish at $w$: the map of residue fields $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(w)$ is injective, so it preserves and reflects zero. Thus the pulled-back functions satisfy exactly the original coordinate hypothesis on the regular locally Noetherian scheme $W$. Steps 1--4, applied to these functions, prove all the same assertions there, with $D_W$ and $C_W$ given by the pulled-back product and ideal. Their branch count is $|I_u|=b(\bar u)$, proving invariance under etale neighborhoods as well as all the asserted base-change statements.

split_report.summary: Split the coordinate branch-count lemma without creating nodes: parameter quotients and strict henselization identify its branch primes; faithful-flat contraction proves their incomparability; coordinate quotient rings give the regular reduced center; finite counting gives closed multiplicity loci; etale maximal-ideal generation and dimension transport the hypothesis. The statement is unchanged. Added the existing reduced-scheme definition as a statement dependency.
split_report.blueprint: This descendant of lem-trf-local-term-locality realizes the coordinate-stratum input in Step 1 and Step 2 of lem-trf-nc-maximal-branch-blowup, on the existing alteration/normal-crossings branch below the ancestor specialization step. In ILO VIII 4.1.6 and 4.1.8, the multiplicity stratification and regular deepest stratum are expanded by Steps 1--4; Step 5 verifies the etale coordinate passage used there. No unit or chapter route changes.

tool_uses.why: The general local presentation relates the pointed-etale geometric strict local ring to the algebraic strict henselization of the ordinary local ring; it is needed before applying the algebraic quotient theorem.
The general parameter-quotient theorem supplies regular local quotients and nonzerodivisors; it is the local algebra needed by the coordinate normal-crossings argument.
The general quotient theorem identifies the strict local rings of the coordinate hypersurfaces and of the divisor; this unit has no replacement for that algebraic identification.
Regularity of strict henselizations makes the coordinate hypersurface quotients regular local.
Regular local quotients are domains, giving prime coordinate ideals and reducedness of the center.
Faithful flatness allows comparison of the parameter ideals before and after strict henselization.
Contraction of extended ideals preserves incomparability of distinct parameter ideals.
General Noetherian ascent supplies locally Noetherian etale neighborhoods.
The general etale local-ring theorem transports generators of the maximal ideal.
The general etale dimension theorem ensures that the transported parameter list has the required length.
